x: The race marked the return of Jack Rutland to racing after a long break, and although he was fairly well down the field, it was pleasing to see him out once again.

Jack Rutland is mentioned in despatches and also G. Warr who is improving quickly, but the hero of the day was Bob Readman who although feeling the effects of the National Police Championship two days previously battled to the finish to score for us.

In a batch at about 5 miles were Jack Bidgood, Charlie Churcher and Fred Redman, all walking very strong. At 18 miles Charlie started to drop back and Jack Rutland came up. Jack walked a very fine and well judged race.

…her unsettled and soon after the start competitors had quite a downpour of rain to contend with, but this did not deter Jack Rutland who set up quite a fast pace and led the field for the first twelve miles when he was caught and passed by Cowley (S.W.C.) who from that point was never headed.…

Jack Bidgood started going up towards the front quite early with Jack Wakeley and Jack Rutland not too far back. Then there followed all in quick succession the remaining five of the “ A ” Team, Don Heath, Hugh McGreechan, “Sir” Harry Shields, Joe Wilson and Dick Frazer.
George Oliver snowed that he will be among ’em, too, in the opens and Jack Rutland, who had been thinking of having a rest, finished third in great style and now thinks resting a waste of time.
Jack Stirling Wakeley and Jack Rutland finished 4th and 5th in the Hastings—Brighton Walk on August 19th and Jack Wakeley was 3rd in the handicap.

After five miles the front positions were the same, and we had Percy Wright lying handy in the first twenty, with Jack Rutland and Bob Readman walking shoulder to shoulder, and Hugh McGreechan, Harry Shields and Jack Bidgood all packing well in that order.
Jack Rutland was in the leading four for 14 or 15 miles, but cramp in his toes forced him to retire after covering 20 miles. Percy Wright was another one who was unfortunate.
Close behind were Jack Rutland, Jack Bidgood, Jack Wakeley and Harry Shields. As early as Croydon, Jack Wakeley showed signs of trouble with his shoes and soon began losing ground.

With Harry Churcher 3rd and Dave McMullen 4th we had another scratch team win despite the fact that we lost George Checkley who was well up at about 3 miles and had to wait until 26th position was filled by Jack Rutland.

Roberts, Jack Rutland, George Checkley, Fred Rickards and Frank Thomson. Frank is particularly mentioned for his tremendous effort in regaling the walkers from first to last with Horlicks and sponging, and it was truly amazing to see such vitality from one of his age.

One of his proudest memories was helping Belgrave to finish 2nd team in a big Open 50Kms. at Eastleigh in 1949. Other scoring members of the team were Jack Rutland and Tommy Green. Joe himself also took third handicap prize and a time standard medal.
The inaugeral R.W.A. 10 miles Championship at Sheffield in 1947 gave Harry another Championship at Sheffield in 1947 gave Harry another Championship win, and with Jack RUTLAND (2), R.D.

After the war our walkers soon got down to things at Belgrave Hall and our winning ways continued and it is no surprise that we won the first National 10 held at Sheffield with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland taking the first two places.
